issues.description: The problem statement (and UML) requires a public method checkOrderReady() on SealSaloon to process and serve ready orders. The reference solution implements this behavior in a method named processOrders() instead of checkOrderReady(), causing a signature/name mismatch between the specification and the solution. This can confuse students about which method to implement and may break any checks or tests that expect the exact method name checkOrderReady().
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the solution method processOrders() to checkOrderReady() (keeping the same behavior), or add a public checkOrderReady() method that delegates to processOrders(). Ensure the method name in the solution matches the method name and UML in problem_statement.md so students implement the expected API.

issues.description: The problem statement requires a method named checkOrderReady() on SealSaloon (used by orderMeal()), but the solution implementation uses a method named processOrders() to perform the same behavior. This naming mismatch between the described API (checkOrderReady) and the reference implementation (processOrders) can confuse students about the required method name and where to implement the order-serving logic.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the solution's processOrders() method to checkOrderReady(), or add a public checkOrderReady() wrapper that delegates to processOrders(), and ensure orderMeal() calls checkOrderReady() so the implementation and the problem statement API names match.
